crm_notes: Summary: Tier-1 network infra provider evaluating Redwood for private VPC inference. Primary driver = tight network controls + auditability.
Workload profile: chat-heavy (conversational assistants to field technicians), embeddings for doc-search, occasional batch reranking for ticket triage.
Throughput & latency targets: steady-state ~50 RPS, burst to 200 RPS, p95 target <200ms for short-chat flows. Cost sensitivity moderate but will trade cost for strong isolation and SLA.

Network requirements (detailed): customer insists on PrivateLink or VPC Peering (preference: PrivateLink for minimal routing overhead). All egress must be customer-managed through their NAT/VPN; no public egress from Redwood-managed IPs unless static IPs provided and allowlist approved.

Firewall & allowlist: Security team needs example inbound/outbound port lists, CIDR ranges for PrivateLink endpoints, step-by-step iptables / cloud firewall config they can hand to ops. Must support per-subnet routing and deny-by-default policies.

Audit logging & retention: Require immutable audit logs for API requests and admin actions, CloudTrail-style events forwarded to customer SIEM (S3 bucket in customer's account preferred). Retention policy requested: 7 years for select audit events.

KMS integration: BYOK with AWS KMS preferred. Customer requires that model cache/kv and snapshot encryption use keys in their account, with Redwood able to perform Envelope Encryption. HSM mention during call - they will escalate if KMS doesn't meet compliance.
Data residency: Primary deployment in us-east-1, but EU residency required for subset of traffic. Want routing policy that pins EU customers to EU-hosted Private deployment and audit segregation.

Model strategy & fallbacks: Prefer running quantized open models (Llama-variant) in Private, but want Redwood's routing/fallback to smaller footprint model if Dedicated capacity constrained. Documented regression testing needed before cutover.
Quote from CTO (A. Rodriguez): 'We can't accept third-party-owned S3 for logs — all telemetry must land in our account or on-prem SIEM. Also, static egress IPs are non-negotiable.'

POC milestones: 1) Network connectivity & PrivateLink proof (week 0-2), 2) KMS BYOK key rotation test (week 2-4), 3) Throughput + latency run (week 4-6), 4) Security signoff + legal addendum (week 6-8).
Notes on procurement: They will push for annual committed capacity if POC meets SLAs. Legal already asked for data residency clause and standard DPA modifications.

Tactical asks for AE/SE: Provide sample VPC peering/PrivateLink CloudFormation templates, recommended firewall rules, and a short whitepaper on audit log delivery options (S3 push vs direct SIEM ingestion).
